speaker: yeung
title: Privacy by design
narration: First, privacy. Staff need crowd patterns, so we chose to process video locally and send numerical observations. Our server accepts a valid reading, rejects one containing an identity field, and refuses image uploads.

speaker: wong
title: Test the counts
narration: On one mall camera, the detector under-counted. After calibrating with twenty labelled frames, held-out error was about three people per frame, versus about five for a fixed guess. This calibration is not yet in the app.
visual: Derived scatter/chart only; no Mall imagery. Compare held-out MAE 3.3 with fixed-count baseline 4.8, static numerals, same scale. One camera / 20 labelled frames / offline calibration / not in app.

speaker: wong
title: Test the warning time
narration: Counting accuracy doesn't guarantee warning time. On held-out simulated days, our fifteen-minute model beat the no-change baseline. But in a fast simulated surge, the first confident warning came about a minute after the alert threshold was crossed. Staff review remains essential. Our adjusted confidence score is a review cue, not a calibrated probability.
visual: Keep the simulated +15-minute scores. Highlight About 1 minute late in the Run A sampled timeline, then show the review UI. Timestamps differ by 59 simulated seconds; sampling is about 30 simulated seconds, so do not imply precise field latency. Prototype threshold is not a safety limit.

speaker: ku
title: Compare a street-change scenario
narration: CrowdPulse also includes scenario simulation, to compare street changes for different mobility needs. In one full-closure stress test, twenty-four of forty simulated wheelchair journeys had no mapped step-free route in either plan. The closure did not create those twenty-four unreachable journeys. Map data and on-site checks still matter.

speaker: wong
title: What the tests taught us
narration: Our tests showed why prediction quality, warning time and route accessibility need separate checks. In CrowdPulse, missing route evidence now blocks approval and leads to a recorded request for an on-site check.
